Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP status and close timing

Jenna —

Quick check-in after yesterday's session. Procurement flagged a few items (SOC2 artifacts and a standard redline to our DPA) that look like they will push the current 10/06 close out 1–2 weeks unless we can accelerate the evidence handoff.

I attached a one-page MAP (v1) and a short risk catalog that lists the specific blockers and owners. Can you confirm: (1) whether your procurement team needs the full SOC2 binder or a subset summary to proceed, and (2) who on your side will own the DPA redline conversation?

If Helios prefers, we can propose a rebaseline target date and offer a short technical canary that limits initial volume while procurement finishes legal — reduces risk on both sides.

Thanks,
Alex

- Option A: Partial go-live (pilot lane) with constrained QPS and a 30-day evaluation. Lower revenue recognition ramp but keeps momentum.
- Option B: Firming a short-term credit/discount (1 month) in exchange for an extended committed start date if legal needs more time.
- Operational ask: can Infra prioritize a limited canary stack in us-west for Helios?

I want to get a one-page proposal to Jenna today so they can table it in procurement/legal.

Thanks —
Alex

Thanks for the context. Quick feasibility notes from infra & commercial:

1) Canary approach — doable. We can stand up a constrained service profile in us-west in 48–72 hours (rate limits + token caps) and expose a separate route for Helios. We'll need a signed canary SOW addendum that outlines traffic quotas and rollback conditions.

3) SOC2 summary — I can pull a controls matrix (redwood-redacted) and a short evidence index. Marissa, can you coordinate the legal redline turnaround and provide the DPA baseline we can present?

If Alex wants, I can draft the one-page mitigation proposal (canary + evidence + suggested credit) and include the risk catalog.

Subject: Updated MAP + mitigation offer (proposed new close 2027-10-14)

Jenna / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick responses this week. Per our internal review we've prepared a concise mitigation package so Helios can keep momentum while procurement/legal finish their review. Attached is MAP_v2 (high-level milestones), the SOC2 evidence summary you requested, and a risk catalog with owners. Summary: 

- Proposed new close date: 2027-10-14 (two-week rebaseline).
- Canary offer: limited production route in us-west for payer pilot (QPS capped at 50 r/s, token cap per request = 4096). Canary window = 30 days with automatic rollback triggers (error rate > 2% on the route or latency > 2.5s p95).
- Commercial: 1 month service credit if final ARR is signed within 90 days of the proposed close (terms in the MAP attachment).
- Legal: attached DPA baseline + redline notes. We're happy to take Procurement's redlines back in DocuSign.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement confirms which SOC2 artifacts suffice (we attached a summary; can provide additional extracts on request).
2) Legal provides DPA redline owner and estimated turnaround (we can triage comments).
3) If Helios accepts, sign the MAP_v2 and DocuSign the canary addendum; infra will provision the route within 72 hours of executed addendum.

DocuSign prefill — https://app.docusign.com/docu/abcd1234
